draft.title: Bitcoin breaks below $75,000 as ETF outflows swell to $2.1 billion
draft.what_happened: Bitcoin has slipped below $75,000 as the spot-ETF sell-off swelled to $2.1 billion, with IBIT alone accounting for 78% of the withdrawals. On-chain, the most patient cohort is capitulating: long-term holders have moved coins at a loss for eight straight days, with their SOPR reading 0.94.
draft.how_we_got_here: The pressure built in stages. ETFs first shed $1.28 billion in the same window the price lost its 50-week line, then the outflow wave grew to $2.1 billion with the largest spot fund leading the exit, while long-term holders joined the selling after weeks of holding through the decline.
draft.what_to_watch: Whether ETF demand returns to defend support, and the upcoming U.S. CPI report, which analysts flag as a key test even if inflation cools. The on-chain picture is split: 1-100 BTC wallets added 14,207 BTC over two weeks, whales moved 2,492 BTC off BitGo and Binance into fresh wallets, and roughly 108,700 non-empty wallets closed in a retail exit some read as a bullish contrary signal.

draft.title: Bitcoin ETFs turn net-negative for 2026 as IBIT's $1.66B drain stretches to seven sessions
draft.what_happened: US spot Bitcoin ETFs have given back $1.1 billion so far in 2026, flipping the full-year tally negative after $25 billion of inflows in 2025. The latest session saw a net $201 million of exits, the third straight down day, and BlackRock's IBIT alone has shed $1.66 billion across seven trading sessions.
draft.how_we_got_here: The drain built through last week: $1.3 billion of net weekly outflows, the heaviest since late June, pushed total complex assets below $100 billion. Even the week's counter-move of roughly $5 billion of holders' coins moving into IBIT hasn't dented the broader redemption streak, which is now concentrated in the complex's largest fund.
draft.what_to_watch: Whether the third consecutive day of exits breaks or extends, whether IBIT's seven-session loss stabilizes or deepens, and how far the 2026 net figure travels past $1.1 billion.

results.name: Ethereum
results.reason: New price lows, a Glamsterdam hold call, a security alert, and split whale behavior — none of it covered by the month-old fees update.

draft.title: Ether breaks below $2,100 as audit concerns and whale crosscurrents build
draft.what_happened: Ether broke below $2,100, down 2.24% intraday, sliding well under the $2.45-2.6K range that had framed its recent trading. The new low lands amid two network-level worries: Ethlabs is urging a hold on the Glamsterdam rollout until audit findings are in, raising the prospect of a delay, and a critical alert warns that Ethereum-related software has been compromised.
draft.how_we_got_here: Old wallets are the story around the lows. A 2015-era whale appears to have sold more than 7,500 ETH from a 37,000-coin stack — a return of up to 156,358% — and a genesis-era wallet that moved millions after roughly a decade drew scam attempts within minutes. Against that selling, BitMine added 9,587 ETH even as price fell, an address dormant for a year picked up $5.4 million worth of ETH, and staking has kept climbing through the slide.
draft.what_to_watch: Whether Glamsterdam slips while audits wrap up, what the compromised-software alert actually points to, and which way old-wallet flows tip next — more dormant selling, or more bottom-fishing like this round's.
